`SSLObject` does not support `suppress_ragged_eofs`. All EOF conditions that violate the TLS protocol are reported by raising `SSLEOFError`.

For comparison, `SSLSocket` defaults to `suppress_ragged_eofs=True`, causing `recv()` to return `b""` for an unexpected EOF; with `False`, it raises the exception instead.

Sources: [Python SSL documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/3.7/Doc/library/ssl.rst#7), [SSL documentation](https://python.github.io/python-docs-fa/library/ssl.html#ssl.SSLContext.set_npn_protocols#8)
